headline: Computational models link chromatin folding to epigenetic memory and X inactivation
label: 3D Genome Structure Modeling
summary: Recent models quantify 3D genome structure from single loci to TADs, linking folding to memory, search kinetics, and Xist regulation.
synthesis: The common thread is physics-based and probabilistic modeling of chromatin organization, where simulation or inference recovers structural quantities from imaging, Hi-C, or polymer representations. A polymer-biophysics model incorporating phase condensates and enzymatic activity simulates restoration of H3K9me3 to explain epigenetic memory, and a multiscale polymer and nucleosome-resolution model of the Xic locus examines loop-extrusion and methylation-driven reorganization of Xist and Tsix during X inactivation. PLOTTED infers single-locus distances from Oligopaint imaging, WaveTAD gives resolution-free hierarchical TAD descriptions, and simulations link TAD compaction to faster protein target search across 8,355 human TADs. A modified Hi-C pipeline links transposable elements to interphase contacts. What is new is quantitative modeling that connects structure to function across scales. The holocentromere pangenome study addresses a distinct question, repeat-array turnover across Rhynchospora.
